page: Amazon Web Services m6idn.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs through hyper-threading. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 with VNNI instructions, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and Intel Total Memory Encryption (TME).

Local physical storage is bundled with the instance, providing a 474 GB NVMe SSD directly attached for fast I/O operations without depending solely on network-attached EBS volumes. The network interface supports a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps. The server operates with zero attached GPUs, directing its computing capacity toward pure x86_64 CPU instructions and local memory bandwidth.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50% across most standard computational workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1641.0 and a multi-core score of 6090.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 11363.05. Memory bandwidth reaches 57.49 GB/sec read and 41.45 GB/sec write on 256MB blocks. In application benchmarks, it processes 7.96 million Redis SET operations per second and handles static web serving throughput at 11.9 GB/sec. Weaknesses emerge in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and larger 7B model LLM inference, where text generation drops to 7.67 tokens per second.

From a cost efficiency and architectural perspective, the m6idn.2xlarge offers a balanced resource footprint combining balanced compute and RAM with built-in high-speed local NVMe storage and solid 12 Gbps networking. It suits relational databases, caching layers, containerized backend services, ETL tasks, and web serving where local low-latency scratch space is essential.
description: Amazon Web Services m6idn.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with an 8-vCPU, 4-core Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It integrates a 474 GB local NVMe SSD and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps without GPU acceleration. Across benchmarks, the instance yields average computational performance, achieving 1641.0 in Geekbench single-core, 6090.0 in multi-core, and 7.96 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Multithreaded decompression and medium-sized LLM processing represent lower-tier performance outcomes. With balanced CPU, memory, fast local storage, and solid networking, it is well suited for database systems, microservice deployments, caching infrastructure, and general web applications needing direct NVMe scratch capacity.
